title: OpenAI Agents API
content:
Build durable cloud agents with a managed Codex harness.
The Agents API gives your application access to the Codex harness through an OpenAI-managed API.
OpenAI manages sessions, orchestration, context compaction, and recovery while your application provides tools and chooses its execution environment.
Agents can operate in a sandbox where they can execute code, edit files, connect to MCP servers, and produce artifacts.
Pricing
Model usage is billed at the selected model’s API rates. OpenAI tools use their standard rates, and OpenAI-hosted sandboxes use standard container rates.
Document reviewer: review documents with policy skills and specialist agents.
Core concepts
The Agents API is built around four main concepts:
Agent: The model, instructions, tools, and MCP servers available to the agent.
Environment: An optional sandbox or computer where the agent accesses files, loads skills, and runs commands.
Session: A durable instance of an agent that works on tasks and responds to input.
Events and items: The inputs sent to an agent and the output produced during a session.
A session from start to finish
Start with an OpenAI-hosted sandbox in the quickstart:
Create a session. Configure the agent; OpenAI provisions its environment.
Give it a task. User input starts a turn of work once the environment is ready.
Follow progress. Stream output or use webhooks to learn when the agent finishes or needs input.
Continue or steer. Send another task to the same session, or guide the agent during its current turn.
With an OpenAI-hosted session, your application sends input and receives events, while OpenAI runs the agent and provisions and manages its sandbox. See environment options for setup and limitations.
What the managed harness provides
The managed Codex harness supports:
Running commands and code in a sandbox.
Applying relevant skills and instructions.
Connecting to external data through tools or MCP.
Steering the agent while it works.
Summarizing previous work to manage its context window.
Breaking work into subtasks and delegating to subagents.
Resuming a session where it left off.
Check the quickstart prerequisites for API-key permissions and SDK setup. Configure these capabilities when you create a session:

report.summary: OpenAI's Agents API offers a managed Codex harness for building durable cloud agents with sessions, sandboxes, MCP tools, subagents, and recovery.
report.background: Agentic AI has moved from demos to production, but builders still stitch together orchestration, sandboxing, memory, context-window management, and recovery. OpenAI's Agents API packages its Codex harness as a managed service, following the industry trend toward hosted agent runtimes from cloud and model providers. It targets applications that need durable, steerable agents that can run code, edit files, connect to MCP servers, and produce artifacts. Rather than only offering chat completions or function calling, OpenAI now manages the session lifecycle. This reflects competition with frameworks like LangGraph and AutoGen and cloud services like Bedrock Agents and Vertex Agent Builder. It also standardizes MCP as a tool connectivity layer. Pricing follows model, tool, and container rates. The docs emphasize OpenAI-hosted or self-hosted environments, positioning the API for both quick prototypes and controlled enterprise deployments.
key_points: The Agents API gives applications access to OpenAI's Codex harness as a managed service. OpenAI handles sessions, orchestration, context compaction, and recovery, while developers supply tools and choose execution environments. Agents can run in sandboxes where they execute code, edit files, connect to MCP servers, and produce artifacts.

Four core concepts organize the API: Agent (model, instructions, tools, MCP servers), Environment (optional sandbox or computer for files, skills, and commands), Session (durable instance that works on tasks and responds to input), and Events/items (inputs and outputs during a session).

A session follows a simple lifecycle: create a session, give the agent a task, follow progress via streaming or webhooks, then continue or steer the same session. OpenAI-hosted sessions provision and manage the sandbox; self-hosted environments let teams control workspace directories and capabilities.

The managed harness supports running commands, applying skills and instructions, connecting to external data via tools or MCP, steering agents mid-work, summarizing previous work for context management, delegating subtasks to subagents, and resuming sessions where they left off.

Pricing uses selected model API rates, standard rates for OpenAI tools, and standard container rates for OpenAI-hosted sandboxes. Example use cases include document review with policy skills and specialist agents, plus multi-agent research with configurable concurrency.
report.impact: For the AI industry, OpenAI's Agents API turns agent orchestration into a first-class managed cloud primitive. It could pressure standalone frameworks and cloud rivals to differentiate on openness, portability, and governance, while validating MCP as a standard tool layer. Developers gain faster paths to durable, sandboxed agents without building session stores, context compaction, recovery, or sandbox lifecycles, but should weigh vendor lock-in, cost, and data residency. Regular users should see more reliable long-running assistants that can research, review documents, and complete multi-step tasks with less babysitting. Enterprises may pair hosted sandboxes with self-hosted environments for control.
report.tools: Follow OpenAI's Agents API docs, Agents SDK, and Codex harness examples. For tool connectivity, watch Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and OpenAI-hosted or self-hosted sandboxes. Open-source alternatives and complements include LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenHands, E2B, and Daytona for agent orchestration, sandboxing, and durable execution. Compare governance and portability before committing.
